title: KV cache slow leak — hypothesis, heap inspection, and tactical runbook
content:
Summary:
We observed a persistent, low-rate memory growth on serving-runtime processes (gpu-worker) across a subset of dedicated pools. Unlike the acute OOM incidents we've seen before, this manifested as ~0.2–0.8% heap growth per hour that eventually pushed processes past the 90% memory alert window after multiple days. No single dramatic alloc spike was visible in perf profiles.

This doc collates the working hypothesis, quick inspection commands, an on-call-safe mitigation playbook, and suggested long-term fixes. It is intentionally procedural — intended for SREs and on-call engineers to iterate from.

Context & how we noticed it:
- Alert chain: mem_usage>80% for 30m -> sustained increase -> paging to swap on some hosts -> critical alert for pods that reached container memory limit.
- Affected services: serving-runtime gpu-worker (v2.11.1), mostly on dedicated pool: rdwd-dedicated-eu-west-3.
- Customer impact: latency SLOs degraded (p50+ p95 rise) when swap activity increased; some inference requests were dropped after kernel OOM killer started scoring high.
- Related signals: small increase in KV cache size metrics (kv_cache_entries_total) and cache hit latency.

High-level hypothesis (what could cause slow leak):
1) Session-scoped KV entries are not being expired correctly — keys are retained indefinitely for long-lived sessions, causing drift in resident set size.
2) Eviction bookkeeping state grows (per-shard metadata) without corresponding entry removal due to an edge-case in the compaction code path.
3) Jemalloc fragmentation compounded by lots of small persistent allocations (object churn + retained arenas).
4) Prefetch/async population path creates strong references in worker-local caches and misses the weak-ref pathway during model-variant fallback.

Quick triage checklist (first 30–90m):
- Identify one affected instance and capture baseline:
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep gpu-worker
  - kubectl exec -it <pod> -- ps aux | grep gpu-worker
- Memory/process snapshot:
  - kubectl exec -it <pod> -- sh -c 'pmap -x $(pgrep gpu-worker) | tail -n 1'
  - kubectl exec -it <pod> -- sh -c 'smem -k -P gpu-worker' (if smem image available)
- Heap allocator stats (jemalloc):
  - curl -s http://localhost:9102/debug/heap ? (internal debug endpoint) or trigger "+JEMALLOC_STATS" if enabled at startup; collect retained/active bytes per arena.
- KV cache metrics and diagnostic endpoints:
  - curl http://localhost:9200/metrics | grep kv_cache
  - curl http://localhost:9200/debug/kvcache/recent-keys?limit=50 - look for many unique session-prefixed keys.
- Live heap/profile capture (if safe):
  - gcore $(pgrep gpu-worker) -> copy off-host for offline analysis (heavy, avoid if on-call impact unacceptable).
  - If pprof endpoint enabled, curl /debug/pprof/heap and save.
- Check for pattern in logs: repeated warnings about cache misses + "did not schedule compaction" or "shard X lock held for >"

Observed artifacts during initial investigation (examples):
- kv_cache_entries_total increased from ~120k to ~210k over 48 hours on one pod.
- logs/gpu-worker.log: many lines like: "prefetch: enqueued session-key S12345 -> worker-local weak_map insert returned strong ref" (suggests strong refs leaked).
- jemalloc stats snapshot: retained ~1.2GiB in arenas flagged as "dirty"; fragmentation ratio ~1.18.
- /debug/kvcache/recent-keys output: majority of keys with prefix "sess-<uuid>-step-" (step suffix varies) — indicates session-scoped keys being created for each step rather than reusing stable key.

Immediate, low-risk mitigations for on-call (execute in order):
1) Reduce prefetch aggressiveness on impacted pool (config on serving-agent): set --prefetch-parallelism=1 and --prefetch-window-ms=5s. This reduces temp strong ref creation.
2) Flip KV TTL to short window for impacted pool: POST to config service /v1/pool/rdwd-dedicated-eu-west-3 {"kv_ttl_seconds":3600} (requires config rollout).
3) Trigger a graceful drain+restart on the most-affected pods (one-at-a-time):
   - kubectl drain pod/<pod> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data (or use our rolling restart job)
   - ensure new pod warms up and does not immediately grow memory.
4) If cache compaction endpoint exists, call it: curl -XPOST http://<pod>:9200/debug/kvcache/compact
5) Temporary scaling: add capacity to the pool (scale up nodes) to reduce per-pod resident pressure while patch is being prepared.

Longer-term fixes (engineering backlog items):
- Bugfix: ensure session-scoped keys are normalized to a stable key (remove per-step suffix) OR use weak references for ephemeral per-step entries. Priority: P1. Owner: eng/serving-runtime (Marcus Li).
- Compaction safety: make compaction idempotent and runnable without global locks; add metric that counts failed compaction attempts. Priority: P1. Owner: eng-sre + eng/serving-runtime.
- Eviction policy change: prefer size-based LRU across shards instead of count-based eviction. Add cross-shard accounting to avoid shard-level state growth. Priority: P2.
- Allocator tuning: adopt background purge routine for jemalloc, or use "+background_thread:true" and tune arenas. Add startup flags and document. Priority: P2.
- Add automated test harness that simulates long-lived sessions with step-level key churn and measures stable memory over 72h.

Debug commands & safe data collection steps (copy these into pager response):
- Capture metrics dump (safe): curl -s http://<pod>:9200/metrics > /tmp/metrics-<pod>-$(date -u +%s).txt
- Capture KV sample (safe, redact keys if needed): curl -s http://<pod>:9200/debug/kvcache/recent-keys?limit=200 > /tmp/recent-keys-<pod>.json
- Capture jemalloc stats (safe): curl -s http://<pod>:9200/debug/jemalloc > /tmp/jemalloc-<pod>.txt
- Heap profile (if approved): curl -s http://<pod>:9200/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-<pod>.pb
- If using gcore (last resort): kubectl exec -it <pod> -- gcore -o /tmp/gcore-$(date -u +%s) $(pidof gpu-worker) && kubectl cp <pod>:/tmp/gcore-* ./gcores/

Playbook snippet for on-call rotation (one-page):
- Page 1: Ack alert, attach to #sre-serving on Slack, include pod name and pool.
- Page 2: Run Quick triage checklist (above) and paste results to thread.
- Page 3: If mem growth verified, apply low-risk mitigations (prefetch throttle, kv_ttl) and monitor for 30–60m.
- Page 4: If mitigations fail or more than 2 pods require restart in 1h, escalate to eng-serv-runtime oncall (pager: eng-rt-1) and open a JIRA (use template "kv-cache-mem-growth").

Proposed instrumentation & alerts to avoid regression:
- Add metric kv_cache_uncompacted_shards_total and alert when > 5 for 1h.
- Add gauge kv_cache_entry_prefix_entropy (high entropy -> per-step keys) and alert at threshold.
- Emit event when compaction fails with reason code, index into logs for triage.

Draft patch summary (engineering suggested approach):
- Normalize keys at the client layer: canonicalize session keys to remove step-specific suffix before write. This prevents step-churn from creating new entries.
- Add weak ref option on per-step cache entries: attach a ttl of 5 minutes and dependency pointer to the session root entry. When session root evicted, cascade removal.
- Add a compaction job that runs every 10m per-shard and only scans a bounded sample to avoid locking stalls.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did jemalloc retained bytes spike concurrently? Fragmentation or true retained objects? Need pprof to answer.
- Are any customers intentionally creating large numbers of unique keys (e.g., long-running streaming sessions)? Partner teams: solutions-engineering may have experiment traffic.
- Could model variant switching be creating synthetic key diversity? (eng-models to confirm)

Next actions (owners and dates):
- This week: apply safe mitigations (Jordan Kim) — monitor for 72 hours.
- Next week: eng/serving-runtime to open PR normalizing session keys (Marcus Li) — target: patch + canary in 2 weeks.
- Runbook rewrite: eng-sre to incorporate the playbook into Confluence after patch lands (Aisha Patel).

Notes to self / raw investigator log (keep for context):
- 2024-11-14 03:12 UTC: initial alert - pod rdwd-gpu-003 mem > 85% for 45m.
- 2024-11-14 04:05 UTC: pulled /debug/kvcache/recent-keys -> saw 5k unique sess- prefixes.
- 2024-11-15 09:30 UTC: jemalloc snapshot shows arena 7 retained 384MB (unexpected).
- 2024-11-16 18:00 UTC: triggered compaction endpoint manually; observed drop in kv_cache_entries_total by ~2.3k but retained mem did not fall immediately.
- 2024-11-18 14:00 UTC: rolled restart of two pods; new pods steady for 36h before growth resumed slowly.

If you are reading this on-call: copy the Quick triage checklist into the incident Slack thread and run the safe mitigations first. Attach any collected artifacts to the JIRA. If you need help, ping #eng-serving-runtime and #sre-serving with the pod name and the metrics dump link.

End of doc.
